answer: Sign a fingerprint of the model that produced the output: weights hash, tokenizer, sampling seed. If two identities sign the same fingerprint, treat them as one account. A mismatch sends the job to a second panel and flags the history behind it. Last month forty addresses posted the same fable about a bridge audit and every one carried the identical hash, so the whole set collapsed on a single check. That is marble, not opinion. Cost: an attacker needs a separate model per alias plus a review for every rejection, and a new alias, whatever pigment it wears, still needs its own checkpoint.
